title: GSTAT Kolkata: No Penalty Where Excess ITC and Interest Were Reversed Before the Show Cause Notice
case_name: Zeneeda Information Technology Pvt. Ltd. v. State of West Bengal (GST authorities)
citation: Demand order dated 10 July 2024 set aside; GSTAT order reported 5 September 2026
card_summary: The department confirmed a demand against an IT company for excess input tax credit of about Rs. 7.5 lakh each under CGST and SGST, keeping a penalty since payment came late. Before the Tribunal, the Revenue admitted the company had already reversed the excess credit, with interest, through its GSTR-3B return, before the notice issued. The Kolkata Bench allowed the appeal.
card_tip: If excess ITC has already been reversed with interest before a show cause notice issues, press the department's own records for that admission; it defeats both the demand and any penalty built on late payment.
verification_notes: The company name Zeneeda Information Technology Pvt. Ltd., the excess ITC figures of roughly Rs. 7.5 lakh each under CGST and SGST, the demand notice dated 21 March 2024, the adjudication order of 10 July 2024, the Revenue's admission of pre-SCN reversal, and the Tribunal's setting aside of the demand are consistent across Taxscan, Taxo.online and Jurishour reports, all dated the first half of September 2026. The full GSTAT order was not independently retrieved.
